dossier.architecture: Inverted swerve, actively positioned collector and turreted shooter with rotating traversal climb.

subsystems.drivetrain: WCP inverted swerve chosen for packaging and low motor placement.
subsystems.intake: Motor-controlled low collector catches bouncing cargo; side impact guards protect centering wheels.
subsystems.transfer: Printed guide, staging limit switch and color sensor feed the shooter.
subsystems.scoring: Turret on routed gear; operator sequencing/shot tuning emphasized.
subsystems.endgame: Spring deployment plus rotating arm, latching hooks and servo-released retention transfer between rungs.
subsystems.controls: Color rejection through an alternate shot; climb sequence manages when hooks are locked or released.

versions: Side guards added after walls damaged foam wheels. Multiple collector prototypes preceded final geometry.
dossier.analysis: The latches are essential to the rotating climb, and the collector must retract clear of it. Preserve those interaction constraints when comparing apparently similar rotating climbers.
limits: Only published/reviewed configurations are established; further intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2022-148 · Low hardware placement and staged turret feeding share scarce volume
context_documents.body:
# 2022-148: Low hardware placement and staged turret feeding share scarce volume

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

An inverted swerve arrangement moves motors low, while a protected collector and printed guide feed staged cargo to the turret. A limit switch and color sensor support possession/rejection. The climb uses retained hooks and a rotating arm.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team identifies top-side packaging space as a reason for the inverted modules. More exact collector optimization intent remains in the retained source bundle rather than the selected excerpt.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Lower motors can free the turret/feed envelope without eliminating service and cable constraints. Color detection and staged possession need separate states so a delayed classification cannot feed the wrong cargo.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test sensor latency, partial entry and turret-angle transfer clearance; verify climb hard-stop and disabled retention.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: Robowranglers team interview at Texas Championship
source_reviews.locator: 1:30–2:38 drive; 2:40–4:29 pickup; 4:30–6:55 index and turret; 6:56–9:00 climb
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
source_reviews.facts: Team describes inverted swerve, intake wheel protection, a limit-switch index position, color handling and servo-release hook locks.
source_reviews.limitations: Interview gives conflicting estimates of turret travel. No numeric angle or motor count inferred.

source_reviews.title: Robowranglers Quickdraw reveal
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team announcement and later question
source_reviews.facts: Post 1 identifies Quickdraw and early schedule. Post 13 asks about shooter power and wheels.
source_reviews.limitations: The reader question cannot establish installed hardware details.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Quickdraw was a swerve-driven cargo cycler with a low reaching collector, color-aware transfer, yawing launcher and rotating traversal climber. The inverted drive module orientation made better use of volume above the chassis in a season with limited obstacle crossings. The climb occupied a sector that the launcher could face but that the team identified as unusable for shots.
source_review.piece_flow: The collector gets low over bouncing cargo, maintains contact across several rollers and guides the ball inward. A printed transfer part with a Velcro contact surface moves cargo into the index position, where a limit switch stops movement and a color sensor classifies it. Correct cargo proceeds to the launcher. The team describes mostly ejecting opposing cargo upward through the shooter.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Inverted Swerve X places the Falcons lower. The collector has mechanically controlled deployment so it can retract for hangar clearance. The turret and climber share a region in the upper package, so useful aim is a function of mechanical position and safe shot geometry.

subsystems.name: Drive and operator
subsystems.construction: Inverted Swerve X modules with low motor packaging.
subsystems.operation: Swerve supports lateral escape and translation while the turret aims.
subsystems.team_rationale: Save vertical space when repeated obstacle crossings were limited and preserve maneuverability under defense.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Measure bottom clearance and protection at the worst obstacle approach. The driver still needs practice to turn independent translation into usable scoring time.
subsystems.interfaces: Bumper height, motor protection, floor obstacles and heading control.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect underbody impact marks and connections after crossings.
subsystems.unknowns: Drive reduction, clearance and loaded acceleration.

subsystems.name: Intake and transfer
subsystems.construction: Low multi-roller intake with foam outer wheels, added side guards and a printed transfer element carrying Velcro.
subsystems.operation: Multiple contacts keep cargo moving toward the switch-defined queue location.
subsystems.team_rationale: Low pickup controls rebound. The team chose mechanical deployment for more control and to retract for hanging.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The surface needs enough traction to advance cargo and enough compliance to release it. A guard that protects a side wheel can become the first obstacle an oblique cargo sees.
subsystems.interfaces: Roller-to-transfer gap, bumper, limit switch and color sensor.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check side-wheel damage, Velcro wear, switch hysteresis and accumulation at the inside corner.
subsystems.unknowns: Drive details, queue capacity and jam-clear sequence.

subsystems.name: Scoring and rejection
subsystems.construction: A shooter mounted on a routed turret gear and a color sensor at the index point.
subsystems.operation: The drive team reports using the launcher to eject opponent cargo in a different direction.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team emphasizes time spent tuning the indexer and shot together.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Treat the forbidden firing sector as a state constraint. In a fixed-azimuth transfer, chassis heading and reject trajectory need independent validation.
subsystems.interfaces: Indexed cargo position, turret envelope and climber interference.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test false classifications and shot commands across the blocked sector.
subsystems.unknowns: Precise turret travel, shooter layout and firing interlocks.

subsystems.name: Traversal climber
subsystems.construction: Spring-assisted deployment from a stowed position and bar-triggered hooks released with linear servos.
subsystems.operation: Begin at the second rung, rotate to capture the next rung and repeat through traversal. Bar contact triggers the clamp, and the servo moves a release panel.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team describes positively retaining the bar during rotation and releasing once transfer is intended.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Test latch closure under bar misalignment and swing. The release actuator should be tested both unloaded and with residual load at transfer.
subsystems.interfaces: Stow restraint, deployment springs, rung contact, clamp, servo and chassis CG.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test one-sided engagement, incomplete opening and spring rebound at full deployment.
subsystems.unknowns: Quantified load path and safe release criteria.

revisions: Team added side guards called finger guns after repeated wall contact damaged side foam wheels. The March reveal post identifies Quickdraw and initial events, while the captioned interview describes its later Texas configuration.
transferable_principles: Protect the wear part without creating a new capture obstruction. Keep the bar latch and its release as distinct functions.
disconfirming_conditions: A low motor package loses value if the next field demands high obstacle clearance. A rotating climber becomes unreliable if the next bar is outside its loaded capture envelope.
remaining_gaps: Older dossier used for navigation. No verified Quickdraw source code, dimensioned model, or measured cycle dataset. The reveal thread shooter reply is a reader question.
recommended_images: Use the reveal post 1 full-robot images for overview and a dated Texas interview frame near 8:27 for the latch and release linkage.
